summary: This benchmark evaluates an early-exit feature approximation (block 10 of 28 in Qwen2.5-Coder-7B) to drive a 32-coordinate transplant bridge into Qwen2.5-14B on a 512-group Python repair evaluation. Although the early map matches the full late-feature arm at 166/512 completions, its 4.49 percentage point margin over a shuffled-target control fails the pre-registered decision criteria (requiring >=5.0 points with a positive lower bound). The study is an exemplary, honest report of a negative result with rigorous statistical gating.
strengths: Adheres strictly to a pre-registered statistical gate, honestly reporting when the experimental intervention failed to meet prespecified thresholds.
Comprehensive control suite including intact specialist, full teacher features, shuffled target rows, host baseline, and zero ablation.
Detailed reporting of paired statistics, overlap counts, and relative mean squared error separating representation fidelity from downstream behavioral outcomes.
Thorough documentation of hardware specifications, runtime, memory allocation, and software library versions.
weaknesses: Evaluated exclusively on a single synthetic task (bracket decoy completion triplets in Python strings and comments), limiting generalizability to wider coding or reasoning domains.
Explores only a single donor cut (block 10) and one fitting technique (ridge regression) rather than sweeping multiple layer depths or non-linear mapping methods.
suggestions: Evaluate early-exit mapping across multiple intermediate layers (e.g., blocks 8, 12, 16) to establish a depth-versus-repair trade-off curve.
Test the bridge on established, standard code generation benchmarks (such as HumanEval, MBPP, or SWE-bench Lite) to verify if the gate failure is task-specific.

claims.text: FitNets provides a precedent for regressing internal teacher features.
The 23-group early-map advantage was 4.49 percentage points (95% paired interval −0.20 to +8.79), missing the prespecified five-point and positive-lower-bound requirements.
claims.source: Calculated: 23 / 512 = 0.04492 (4.49 percentage points); paired confidence interval crosses zero.

claims.text: Use the previously learned 32-coordinate bridge from Qwen2.5-Coder-7B to Qwen2.5-14B.
claims.source: https://qwen.ai (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and Qwen2.5-14B open model specifications)
